title: Ganjang Pork Bulgogi
shortDescription: Thin pork shoulder is marinated with soy sauce, pear, onion, garlic, and sesame, then grilled in uncrowded batches.
culturalContext: Dwaeji bulgogi describes seasoned pork in a range of Korean preparations. This soy-based, nonspicy version is distinguished editorially as ganjang pork bulgogi; cuts, sweetness, vegetables, and cooking methods vary.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill

ingredients.preparation: partially chilled and thinly sliced across the grain

mixOrder: Combine soy sauce, pear, onion, and rice syrup.
Stir in garlic, scallions, sesame oil, and pepper.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Nonreactive covered container at or below 40°F / 4°C
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 8 hours without test-cook approval; thin pork may become overly seasoned.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve any serving sauce before the marinade contacts raw meat.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard marinade that contacted raw meat; do not brush it onto cooked food.
substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying every label.
Firm ripe pear or unsweetened pear purée may be compared during test cooking.

instructions.heading: Prepare safely
instructions.action: Slice the partially chilled pork on a dedicated board, keep it cold, and wash hands after handling.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices are even and remain cold.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep raw pork and juices away from ready-to-eat foods.

instructions.heading: Mix the marinade
instructions.action: Stir all marinade ingredients until evenly combined.
instructions.safetyNote: Reserve any serving sauce before raw-meat contact.

instructions.heading: Marinate under refrigeration
instructions.action: Coat pork evenly, cover, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Every piece has a thin, even coating.
instructions.safetyNote: Never marinate meat at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Preheat the grill
instructions.action: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill; establish the heat zones described below.
instructions.temperature: Medium-high heat with an open cooler zone
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The grate is hot, clean, and lightly oiled.
instructions.safetyNote: Never use a fuel-burning grill indoors; follow electric-grill ventilation instructions.

instructions.heading: Grill and verify
instructions.action: Shake off heavy excess marinade and grill in uncrowded batches, turning often, until browned and representative thick pieces reach at least 145°F / 63°C.
instructions.temperature: Medium-high heat with an open cooler zone
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The thickest representative pieces reach 145°F / 63°C before a full 3-minute rest.
instructions.safetyNote: Whole cuts of pork require 145°F / 63°C followed by a 3-minute rest.

instructions.heading: Rest and serve
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean platter, apply only clean reserved sauce if used, and rest 3 minutes before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The meat has completed the stated rest on a clean platter.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean utensils and do not return cooked meat to the raw-meat platter.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or approved indoor electric grill with a medium-high direct zone and open cooler zone; cook in uncrowded batches and separate raw and cooked tools.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest representative pieces, followed by a 3-minute rest for whole-cut pork.
visualDonenessCues: Slices are no longer wet with raw marinade
foodSafetyNotes: Keep pork refrigerated at or below 40°F / 4°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify labels and prevent cross-contact.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying every label.
Firm ripe pear or unsweetened pear purée may be compared during test cooking.
ingredientSourcing: Choose cold intact pork shoulder and a ripe fragrant Korean or Asian pear.
makeAhead: Mix marinade up to 2 days ahead; marinate pork only within the stated refrigerated range.
storage: Refrigerate cooked meat in a shallow covered container within 2 hours and use within 4 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat only the needed portion to 165°F / 74°C until steaming; avoid repeated reheating.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers in rice bowls or lettuce wraps within the approved window.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice, lettuce wraps, and crisp banchan.

faq.question: Is this spicy?
faq.answer: This draft is soy-based and contains no chile; Korean pork bulgogi styles vary.

faq.question: Why cook in batches?
faq.answer: Crowding traps steam and prevents controlled browning.

metaDescription: Make soy-based ganjang pork bulgogi with pear, garlic, sesame, refrigerated marination, thermometer checks, and a three-minute rest.
sourcesAndEditorialNotes: Soy-based pork bulgogi is an editorial synthesis compared with the project’s cited bulgogi conventions; exact locked-title framing requires Korean food-editor review.
